description:
FOUND s470bw (2026-09-06) while building #1261's reproducer.

`pcl -I DIR prog.pl` passes `-I DIR` to the perl that runs `pl2cl` for the
PROGRAM (pcl:132 `my @inc_args = map { ("-I", $_) } ($ROOT, @inc_dirs)`), and
Pl::Parser's `inc_paths` defaults to `[PCL lib/, @INC]` â i.e. pl2cl's own
@INC.  But when the RUNTIME transpiles a module it spawns
`perl <pl2cl> --module <path>` (`p-transpile-file`) with NO -I at all, so DIR
is not on that child's @INC.

CONSEQUENCE: a module A in DIR that says `use B` (B also in DIR) is transpiled
with B UNRESOLVED, so `_extract_module_prototypes` returns undef and every
parse fact B carries is missing â SILENTLY.  Measured s470bw with
A2 = `sub go { return blk { 42 } } sub go2 { return join("|", zap, 1) }`:
  pcl -I DIR              -> ":1 zap|1"   (block VALUE passed; bareword string)
  PERL5LIB=DIR pcl -I DIR -> "CODE:1 ZAP|1" = perl's answer
PERL5LIB works only because `p-transpile-file`'s child inherits the
environment.  Nothing warns.

FIX SHAPE (not taken here â it CHANGES MODULE EMISSION wherever a dependency
becomes resolvable, which corpus-diff cannot see; it needs its own sweep + the
CPAN board): pass the runtime's own @INC to the module transpile, e.g.
`perl -I<each @INC entry> <pl2cl> --module <path>`, so a module's transpile-time
search path is the one the runtime will actually use at load.  Check first
whether that widens what `_extract_module_prototypes` reads on the perl-tests
and cpan populations (the gate-SET rule applies: this WIDENS a resolver).

Guard when taken: Pl/t/module-fasl-cache-01.t's run_pcl currently sets
PERL5LIB=$dir with a comment naming this task; that line comes out.

=== DONE (s473i) ===
SHIPPED 2026-09-08.  Both halves.

(1) %p-transpile-inc-args passes THIS program's @INC to the child as -I, so a
module's transpile-time search path is the one the program will load from.
Probe (the task's own A2/B2 shape):
    perl -I DIR                CODE:42 ZAP|1
    pcl  -I DIR    before      VAL:42  ZAP|1
    pcl  -I DIR    after       CODE:42 ZAP|1

MINUS PCL'S SHIM lib/, and that is not a detail: it holds Errno.pm,
Config.pm, POSIX.pm, Carp.pm â modules PCL transpiles but real perl cannot
load â and the first version of the fix killed pl2cl outright:
    panic: Can't use %! because Errno does not define _tie_it
DO NOT RETRY *p-core-inc-dirs* AS THE FILTER (the second wrong attempt,
measured inert): it is pl2cl's whole @INC, so under `pcl -I DIR` it CONTAINS
DIR and filtering on it drops exactly the directory this task is about.  The
test is the shim dir alone, compared as TRUENAMES (@INC spells it <root>/lib,
the derivation <root>/cl/../lib/).

(2) THE CACHE.  "B did not resolve" is a fact the emission encodes, so the
manifest's `missing<TAB>mod<TAB>NAME` record â written since #1261 and until
now parsed and IGNORED â is re-checked at load through p-find-module-in-inc
(a superset of the child's list, so the check errs only towards a needless
re-transpile).  Probe with A in one directory and B in another, one cache:
    run 1: pcl -I A            entry records `missing mod SplitB`
    run 2: pcl -I A -I B       before VAL:42   (stale entry served)
                               after  CODE:42  = perl
Cost on the live cache: 256 missing records over 5939 entries, max 4 per file,
27 distinct names (Win32, VMS::Stdio â never resolvable here).

Guards: Pl/t/module-fasl-cache-01.t 49 -> 55 rows, and its run_pcl STOPS
setting PERL5LIB=$dir (the workaround this task named).  With that line gone,
11 of the file's 55 rows FAIL on the a9f2a264 extraction â six of them the
dependency rows PERL5LIB had been carrying.

ir-spec Â§9.2b updated (normative): validity gains "no name it recorded as
unresolved resolves now"; the section says what the transpile searches and
what is still NOT covered (a dependency that MOVES).

Bar: gen v2-1140, artifacts regenerated; sweep GATE clean TOTAL 18675 (+0);
CPAN board cold and warm with nothing attributable; corpus-diff and
emission-ab IDENTICAL â both are BLIND to this by construction (they run
pl2cl directly; the change is in how the RUNTIME spawns it).
subject: `pcl -I DIR` / `-I` does not reach a MODULE's own transpile: the runtime spawns `perl pl2cl --module` with no -I, so a module's own `use` does not resolve at transpile time and its dependency's PARSE FACTS are silently lost
